one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company catalyst falls in the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29 window. Q4 FY26 results (Aug 25) and Investor Day (Sep 17, guidance reaffirmed) are done, and Q1 FY27 results come in late November or around Dec 1 (Q1 FY26 was Nov 20, 2025; the supervisor found no company release confirming the Dec 1 date). Both dates are outside the window. The Oct 16 dividend is immaterial. The risks are unscheduled: frontier-lab consumer finance and tax launches ahead of the 2027 season, more sell-side cuts (the mean target fell from $456 to $406 between Jul 31 and Sep 18), and news from the class action. Against that, the company is buying back aggressively near the lows (Q4 FY26: 6.8M shares at about $304; $7.9B authorization left), and the stock is oversold at about 11.6x FY27 EPS. Negative momentum and reversal roughly cancel out. I use a near-symmetric lognormal around $268 with about 14% monthly vol (50%/3.5) and a very slight downward tilt for headline risk. This is essentially unchanged from round 1; the supervisor's findings concern 12-month valuation, not the 1-month window.

fair_value.method: Blend, at 0.45/0.40/0.15, of: a P/E on FY28 SBC-inclusive non-GAAP EPS ($25.0 x 12.5x = $312); a normalized, SBC-burdened FCF yield on FY28 (about $6.0B, or $23.3/share on 258M shares, at 7.5% = $308); and a GAAP P/E cross-check (FY28 GAAP EPS $22.0 x 14x = $308).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (NTM at Sep 2027) non-GAAP EPS including SBC, $25.0 x 12.5x

inputs_detail.input: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance (now includes SBC)

inputs_detail.derivation: At $268, $5B+/yr of repurchases retires 7%+ of 267.2M shares gross. SBC of about $2.0B issues about 2.5-3%, and at low prices dollar-based grants dilute more. FY26's $5.5B only cut diluted shares 2% because it was bought at much higher prices. Q4 FY26 buys averaged $304. I take 3.5%, a little below the supervisor's 4%, because the buyback is partly funded by one-off cash-tax savings and cash that also backs the loan book.

About 5% operating net-income growth plus 3.5% buyback accretion. That is below the supervisor's $25.5 because TurboTax is losing share (units -2% vs IRS self-prepared +1.7%), is guided to only +2-3%, and is cutting DIY ARPC. Mailchimp is flat, and FY27's restructuring-driven margin gain (17% of staff) does not repeat.

The stock trades at about 11.6x FY27 today amid AI-disruption fears. H&R Block, the ex-growth tax comparable, trades at about 6.6x forward, which marks the floor. Mature software with high-single-digit growth warrants mid-teens. 12.5x assumes the AI overhang persists through one tax season but earnings hold.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY26 OCF $8.84B, less the $1.28B one-off OBBBA deferred-tax add-back, less $0.22B capex, less $2.06B SBC = about $5.3B normalized. Grown about 6.5%/yr to about $6.0B in FY28 (excluding the remaining ~$0.7B FY27 cash-tax tailwind, treated as one-off). 258M avg shares = $23.3/share. 7.5% required yield = $310, less about $2/share net debt.

inputs_detail.input: Deferred income tax add-back (OBBBA R&D expensing)
inputs_detail.derivation: Removed as non-recurring. The supervisor confirmed it: cash taxes paid were $281M vs $1,408M in FY25, and the capitalized-R&D DTA fell from $1,895M to $673M. The remaining ~$0.7B benefit in FY27 is also excluded from the run-rate.

$5.3B grown about 6.5%/yr (revenue +9-10% less TurboTax drag and credit costs on the growing loan book). The supervisor's ~$6.5B equates FCF to net income; I haircut that for loan-book working capital.
A premium to a mature-software ~5% yield for terminal risk from AI tax tools, but well below H&R Block's implied ~12-15% because Intuit's GBS segment grows 13-14%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 GAAP EPS $22.0 x 14x (a GAAP cross-check built from my own numbers; Goldman's 15x GAAP framework is used only as a reference)

inputs_detail.derivation: The FY27 midpoint of $20.24 grown about 8.7%, the same growth as my non-GAAP path.
Just under Goldman's 15x Sell-case multiple, reflecting the lower H&R Block floor multiple the supervisor established.

bear.story: The Jan-Apr 2027 tax season confirms share loss: TurboTax units fall again while the IRS self-prepared category grows, and ARPC cuts do not win units back. TurboTax revenue declines, the FY27 guide is cut at Q2 or Q3, and FY28 guidance (Aug 2027) is mid-single-digit. The market moves toward an ex-growth tax multiple (H&R Block is at about 6.6x). About 8x on $22 of EPS.

base.story: The company roughly hits the FY27 guide (revenue +9-10%, EPS about $23). TurboTax is flat to slightly up, and QuickBooks/GBS growth of 13-14% carries the story. Buybacks of about $5B/yr cut the share count about 3.5% net. The multiple stays depressed at about 12.5x FY28 EPS of $25 because one season does not settle the AI question.

bull.story: Tax season shows TurboTax Live/assisted growth and units recovering. The AI partnerships look like distribution, not disintermediation. The multiple re-rates to about 16.5x on $25.5 of EPS, near the ~$405 consensus target.

thesis_break_reason: Around $200 (about 8.7x FY27 guided SBC-inclusive EPS of $23, about an 11% normalized SBC-burdened FCF yield), the market would be pricing a decline in earnings, not just deceleration. The most likely causes: a failed 2027 tax season (TurboTax units down again against a growing self-prepared category, a guide cut at Q2/Q3), or GBS/QuickBooks growth breaking below ~10%. I lowered this from $205 because H&R Block at about 6.6x shows how far an ex-growth tax multiple can fall, so ordinary de-rating can reach lower before it signals broken fundamentals.

Durability of QuickBooks/GBS growth of 13-14% if agentic bookkeeping reaches small businesses

reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor confirmed my main round-1 accounting point: FY26 OCF includes a one-off $1.28B OBBBA deferred-tax benefit (cash taxes were $281M vs $1.41B). It also showed that about $0.7B more lands in FY27, and I exclude that from the run-rate too. I accept two corrections. First, net buyback accretion at $268 is materially higher than the 2% I used. The 10-K shows 6.8M shares bought in Q4 FY26 at about $304, and FY26's 2% reduction came at much higher prices. I now use 3.5% net, slightly under the supervisor's 4% because the buyback leans on one-off tax savings. Second, H&R Block trades at about 6.6x forward, not 8-9x, so the ex-growth floor is lower and the left tail fatter. I also acted on the source-review note that I leaned on sell-side frameworks: the Goldman GAAP leg is now my own FY28 GAAP estimate at 14x, cut to 15% weight. I disagree with the supervisor's FY28 EPS of $25.5 and use $25.0. The IRS-vs-TurboTax data (share loss of about 3.7 points) is a skeptic datum that argues for slower operating growth than the +9-10% revenue guide implies, and FY27's restructuring gains don't repeat. New in-lane evidence cuts both ways. Stifel downgraded to Hold ($275) and the mean target fell 11% in seven weeks, so the sell-side is still cutting. But management terminated all 10b5-1 sale plans in March 2026, which weakens my round-1 insider-selling point (the CEO's January sales predate that). The revised fair value is $310 (from $298). Scenarios: bear $175 / base $310 / bull $420 at 25/50/25, mean about $304. The ladder is a mixture: 85% lognormal with median about $300 and sigma 0.38, plus 15% bear lobe near $195. I then shaded the far left tail slightly fatter for the HRB floor. The result is P(>=268) about 0.555, unchanged: a higher fair value offset by the fatter left tail. Research this round was 3 searches; option data and priors were not consulted.

Accepted higher buyback accretion (3.5% net, 10-K Q4 buybacks at about $304). I stayed below the supervisor's $25.5 because of TurboTax share loss (units -2% vs IRS category +1.7%) and non-recurring restructuring gains.

Normalization confirmed by the supervisor (cash taxes $281M vs $1.41B; DTA $1,895M to $673M); the additional ~$0.7B FY27 tax tailwind is excluded as one-off. I rolled forward to FY28 because the valuation is 12 months out, with a lower share count per the buyback finding.

HRB at about 6.6x shows a de-rated floor can sit lower without a fundamental break; $200 is about 8.7x FY27 EPS, where an earnings decline is priced.
